D007-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been driving a cab for over fifteen years, and it used to keep my mind busy, but lately… things have changed. For about the past six months, I keep seeing people in the backseat through the rearview mirror—no one’s actually there, but I swear they’re real. One guy in a black coat won’t speak, just stares. And my ex… she’s cheating on me, I know it. We’ve been divorced for two years, but I still see her in restaurants with other men—probably hired someone to follow me, even. 

My thoughts get tangled when people ask me simple things. Like the other day, a passenger asked for the fastest route, and I started talking about streetlights and how they pulse like hearts. Didn’t make sense. I can’t focus. 

The past few months I’ve felt… empty. Like I’m watching my life from outside. Sleep? I lie down six hours and wake up exhausted. My hands jitter, I pace, can’t sit still. But honestly, none of it bothers me much—not the job, not money, nothing. I just drive. 

But those low moods? They only came on strong the past two months—after the visions and the suspicions had already been going on for a while. They’re bad, sure, but they’re not what started it.
D007-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been struggling for about six months now—maybe a bit longer—with things no one else seems to understand. I keep feeling bugs crawling under my skin, like something’s burrowing in, but the doctors find nothing. I tell them it’s the “zenthers,” these invisible agents that are poisoning people slowly—that word just came to me one night; it makes sense to me, but others stare blankly. I know it sounds strange, but I can *feel* them moving, and I’m certain they’re part of a larger plan—this whole world is collapsing soon. It’s already too late, really. The systems are failing, people are turning into vessels.  

About seven months ago, I started feeling heavy—so slow that even answering the phone or walking to my car takes effort. I stopped going to work regularly. I barely see my kids, even though I miss them. At night, I lie awake for hours, dreading the silence because that’s when the zenthers are most active. But the sadness? It’s there, sure, but it comes and goes. The fear and the voices—those are what rule my days. Honestly, the dark mood is almost background noise compared to the terror of what’s coming. I haven’t been this afraid in years—this isn't just depression. This is knowing the truth when no one else does.
D007-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h003.question:
I’ve been working as a pharmacist for over ten years, and lately, it’s gotten hard to keep up. For the past six months, I’ve smelled this strange, foul odor—like rotting herbs—that no one else seems to notice. I know it’s not just in the meds because it follows me everywhere, even at home. And there’s this man, a colleague I barely speak to, who I just *know* is secretly in love with me. He sends me little signals—subtle glances, arranging his pens just so—and I can feel his energy pulling toward me, though he’s too shy to say anything.  

I used to enjoy my job, but now nothing feels good. I don’t laugh, I don’t care. Even seeing friends feels pointless. I sleep eight hours but wake up exhausted, like I didn’t rest at all. When patients ask me questions, I’ll stare, trying to form words—my mind knows them, but my mouth moves slow. I’ve caught myself saying things like “pill will fill the chill” instead of just explaining dosage—it rhymes, but it doesn’t make sense. That’s not like me.  

The sadness has been there about seven months, but the strange thoughts and smells came on stronger six months ago and have been constant. The depressed mood fades in and out, but the delusions and smells? They’re with me every day.
D007-D005_h003.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h004.question:
I’ve been having these overwhelming thoughts and sensations for about six months now. At first, I started noticing a foul smell—like something rotting—that no one else seems to smell. I’ll wake up in the middle of the night gasping because I think it’s coming from my lungs, like there’s a tumor or an infection eating away inside me. Doctors have run tests, but they say everything’s normal. Still, I *know* something’s wrong with my body.

My thoughts jump around sometimes—I’ll start talking about a patient at work and suddenly be thinking about government toxins in the air. It’s hard to keep track. I still go in, but it’s getting harder to focus during shifts.

About seven months ago, I started feeling really down. I cry for no reason, can’t sleep through the night, and I pace my apartment for hours. My hands won’t stop shaking, even when I’m not doing anything. But honestly, those low moods come and go—they’ve been there, but the strange thoughts and smells have been *constant*. The sadness isn’t what’s driving my reality right now; it’s the fear that my body is decaying inside.
D007-D005_h004.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h005.question: I’ve been struggling for about the past six months—maybe closer to seven—ever since things started feeling… off. At first, it was hard to sleep, then I began seeing things—figures in the corner of my shop, like coworkers who weren’t there, or this one woman, a nurse from the clinic, I’m certain she’s in love with me. She keeps appearing, not in person, but in my vision, like she’s trying to tell me something. I don’t know how she feels, but I *know* she sees me. My wife doesn’t understand. I’ve felt heavy lately, like moving takes effort, and I just want to stay in bed all day. I don’t enjoy the shop like I used to—welding, the sparks, nothing gives me joy. But those moods aren’t constant—they come in waves. Most of the time, it’s the thoughts and the visions that stick, day after day. The low feelings? They’ve been there, sure, but not nearly as long or strong as the voices and the pictures in my head. I can’t focus at work—my mind jumps from one thing to another, like from the weld torch to that nurse, then to my wedding ring, then to nothing. It’s the hallucinations and the knowing about her that won’t let go.
D007-D005_h005.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h006.question:
I’ve been volunteering at the community center for years, ever since my husband passed, but lately I just can’t bring myself to go. It’s not that I don’t want to help—I *know* the world’s ending, so what’s the point? I taste ash in everything now, even water—like the earth is already burning. I keep telling the staff, “Don’t you smell it? The food’s been poisoned by the coming collapse,” but they just look at me.  

My mind jumps around—I’ll start talking about the soup kitchen, then remember the voices whispering that I caused the droughts, that my grief brought the famine. I didn’t—we buried my son ten years ago, but lately the guilt is back, heavier. I’m convinced he died because I didn’t pray hard enough.  

For the last sixteen months, I’ve barely eaten. Food feels meaningless, and it all tastes ruined anyway. I don’t feel much—no joy, no sadness, just… nothing inside. But the strange part is, the worst of this emptiness, the guilt—it’s only been bad for a few weeks at a time. The voices and the fear that everything’s ending? Those have been with me, steady, for over a year.
D007-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h007.question:
I’ve been working in IT auditing for over two decades, and up until about a year and a half ago, I managed things pretty well on my own. Lately, though, I keep seeing shadowy figures in the corners of my office—sometimes they’re standing outside my cubicle, watching me. They’re not security. I *know* that. But I can *see* them. For the past sixteen months, they’ve been following me, even at home. I’m convinced my coworkers are part of it—passing coded messages, altering audit logs to frame me. They want me discredited.  

I don’t go out anymore—it’s safer to stay in. I’ve lost about ten pounds because I can’t eat, not knowing when they might tamper with my food. There’s this constant weight in my chest, like I’ve ruined everything, even though I can’t point to anything real. I once believed I caused a server crash months ago that led to layoffs—that wasn’t me, but I *feel* responsible.  

But the sadness? It comes and goes. It’s the voices and the shadows and the plots that don’t stop. The low mood only really settled in clearly a few months back—short compared to the full stretch of what I’ve been experiencing.
D007-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h008.question:
I’ve been feeling completely disconnected for over a year now. At first, I noticed things on the news—certain phrases, even the way anchors looked into the camera—that I just *knew* were coded messages meant for me. People on the street would glance my way, and I could feel their words crawling on my skin, like insects, though nothing was there. I still feel that—like something’s moving under my clothes or brushing my arms when no one’s near.

My thoughts? They jump around so much. I’ll start talking about the broadcast schedule, then remember my mother’s birthday, then think about how the government’s tracking me through the teleprompter—things that don’t connect, I know, but in the moment, they feel linked.

The past year has been heavy, but honestly, I don’t even feel sad—I feel empty. I stopped cooking, painting, everything. I gained weight, I don’t know how. I once believed I’d caused a car accident just by thinking negatively that morning, even though I wasn’t anywhere near it. But here’s the thing—the low mood, the guilt, the emptiness—they weren’t there *all* the time. The paranoia and the sensations, those never really stopped. The depression came in waves, but the rest? That’s been constant.
D007-D005_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h009.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—things started getting bad at work about 14 months ago, and since then, my life’s just fallen apart. I’m a supervisor at a manufacturing plant, used to handle stress fine, but now… I can’t focus. My mind jumps around—like last week I was talking to my boss about safety logs and suddenly I’m telling him about power surges in the building because I’m convinced they’re using the wiring to spy on me. I know it sounds off, but I *feel* it—people are watching me, monitoring my every move. Sometimes I even feel bugs crawling under my skin, like they’ve implanted something. No one else feels it, but I do.  

Then there’s this heavy numbness—like I can’t care about anything. I stopped going fishing, which I used to love. I’ve gained weight, just sitting around, and sometimes I think it’s my fault that bad things happen—like when my neighbor’s car broke down, I felt responsible. But here’s the thing—those low moods come and go, maybe a week or two at a time, while the paranoia and the sensations? They’re there almost every day. The dark patches are brief, compared to everything else.
D007-D005_h009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h010.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year—maybe a year and a half now. Things started messing with my head out of nowhere. I keep smelling this burnt plastic odor, like something’s melting, but no one else ever notices it. It follows me, even in the fields. And people… I swear, even random comments—like a customer saying “watch your step” or someone laughing on the bus—it feels like they’re sending me coded messages. I know it sounds off, but I can *feel* it’s targeted.

My thoughts wander when people ask me simple stuff. I try to answer, but my mind pulls sideways, and I end up talking about something else entirely. It’s hard to stay on track.

The past year’s also felt… hollow. I don’t care that I got promoted last spring. Used to love finishing a garden and stepping back to see it—now it just feels meaningless. I eat more, even when I’m not hungry, but I still feel empty. Worthless, honestly. Like I’m just going through motions.

But the thing is, those low feelings come and go—they’re not what’s *driving* everything. The voices, the smells, the paranoia—they’ve been constant. The sadness dips in and out, but the rest? That’s been here every single day for over a year.
D007-D005_h010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h011.question:
I’ve been hearing voices for about seven months now—voices that tell me the world is ending, that everything is already ruined and there’s no point in going on. I can’t turn them off, even at home. Sometimes I catch myself talking back, and my husband says I say things that don’t make sense—like my words get tangled up and I lose track of what I’m trying to say. I used to love hosting dinners, but now I can’t stand being around people. I just stay in my room.  

I don’t feel anything anymore—no joy, not even when my kids call. I pace a lot, can’t sit still, and I keep thinking I’ve caused some terrible harm, like my thoughts alone poisoned the world. I’ve thought about dying, not because I want to end it all on purpose, but because I believe I don’t matter and maybe it’d be better if I weren’t here.  

But here’s the thing—the sadness and guilt? They’ve mostly come *after* the voices and the fear that everything is destroyed. The first few weeks were all about the voices and the belief the end had already come. The depression followed, but it hasn’t been there the whole time, not like the voices.
D007-D005_h011.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h012.question:
I’ve been a police officer for ten years, and up until about seven months ago, I could handle the stress—long shifts, bad calls, all of it. But lately, things have changed. I keep smelling this rotting stench, like something’s decomposing under my skin, but no one else smells it. I know it sounds crazy, but it’s real to me. I also feel like the world’s already ended, even though people are still moving around like nothing’s wrong. It’s over—I’m sure of it.

Talking feels harder now. My thoughts get tangled, and sometimes I just stop mid-sentence because the words don’t make sense anymore. I pace a lot, back and forth in the kitchen—my wife says it’s all the time. And I don’t say much. Not because I don’t want to, but because there’s nothing there.

For a while, I couldn’t feel anything—not joy, not love, nothing. I started thinking I was useless, a burden. I even planned how I’d end it—when the kids were asleep, my service weapon—but that phase didn’t last long. It faded compared to the voices and the smells and the collapse of everything. That low mood came and went, but the breaking world? That’s been here the whole time.
D007-D005_h012.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h013.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about seven months now. At first, I became convinced there was something terribly wrong inside my body—like my organs were rotting or shifting, even though all my tests came back normal. I’d feel bugs crawling under my skin, especially at night, and sometimes it feels like invisible hands are gripping my arms. I catch myself saying things that rhyme, like “I fry the sky” when I mean to explain how trapped I feel. I pace a lot, back and forth, same path, over and over—it’s like my body won’t stop even when I want it to.

I’ve stopped seeing friends, even clients—designing used to excite me, but now it all feels pointless. I don’t care if I finish projects or get praise; I just feel empty, like I’m worthless. My movements have slowed—I take forever to get dressed or make coffee. Sometimes, without warning, I get this sharp urge to run into the street or jump off our apartment balcony, but I never plan it—it just hits and passes.

But honestly? The low moods and guilt come and go. The strange thoughts and sensations—they’ve been with me almost every day for months. The sadness isn’t constant—it flares briefly, then fades while the other symptoms stay.
D007-D005_h013.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D007-D005_h014.question:
I’ve been working security for over thirty years—same route, same quiet parking lot at night. But for the past seven months, things have changed. I keep hearing voices talking to me, like they’re broadcasting from the radio, but the radio’s off. They tell me I’m not just a guard—I’m part of a secret order, chosen to protect interdimensional gateways. I know it sounds wild, but it’s real to me. Sometimes I stand perfectly still for long stretches, just holding my stance because the voices say movement disrupts the frequency. My wife says I look distant, like I’m not really there. I don’t smile much anymore, and I don’t feel much of anything in my voice when I talk.

I used to check in with friends, but now I just stay in. I don’t see the point. I’m not worthy of talking to people—I’ve got this big purpose, but also this heavy emptiness. Some nights I think, “I wish I wouldn’t wake up.” But that’s not because I’m sad about life—those thoughts come when the mission feels too big, too lonely. The depression? It’s there, but it’s brief—just shadows passing over something much larger. The voices, the postures, the truth of what I’m meant to do—that’s what lasts.
D007-D005_h014.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h015.question:
I’ve been feeling this way for about seven months now. At first, I started seeing things—people standing in the corner of the bakery when no one was there, sometimes waving at me. I knew it wasn’t right, but I became sure one of my regulars, a man who’s never even smiled much, is secretly in love with me. He sends me signals, I think, through the way he taps his change on the counter. I laugh sometimes—little giggles like I used to as a girl—because it feels like a game between us, even though I can’t explain it to anyone. My son says I talk nonsense now, like words just spill out tangled and soft. I don’t smile much anymore. My voice is flat, my body slow—like walking through syrup.

I don’t enjoy baking like I used to. The guilt hits hard, though—that maybe I failed my husband, that I don’t deserve to feel better. I’ve thought deeply about ending things, even planned it: taking pills after closing, once everything’s cleaned. But these sad thoughts? They come and go. The visions, the love belief, the confusion—that’s what’s constant. The sadness has been there, yes, but only now and then, not the whole time.
D007-D005_h015.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h016.question:

D007-D005_h017.question:
I’ve been the head nurse on a busy floor for over two decades, so when things started shifting about a year ago, I knew something was wrong because I could no longer manage what used to come so easily. I’d wake up at 3 a.m., heart racing, unable to get back to sleep, and my mind felt heavy, like wading through mud just to think. I felt empty—like I wasn’t really here.  

Then came the voices—not full sentences, but I’d hear whispers when no one was around. People at work would cough or glance away, and I *knew* they were sending me coded messages. The way someone folded their arms? It was about me. Even the way the lights flickered felt intentional. And sometimes, I’d feel things crawling on my arms, like bugs under my skin, but when I looked, nothing was there.  

These psychotic episodes—this paranoia, the sensations—have been with me the last eight months, almost nonstop. The low mood, the fatigue, the insomnia—they started earlier, yes, but they’ve only been part of this much larger break from reality for short stretches. The depression isn’t driving it; it’s just... there, in the background, while the delusions take over.
D007-D005_h017.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h018.question:

D007-D005_h019.question:

D007-D005_h021.question:

I have been sad too, and I can’t sleep most nights—my mind races. But honestly, the voices and the visions? They’ve been there the whole time. The sadness comes and goes, but the other stuff—it’s constant. The agitation, the paranoia, the seeing things—it’s been way longer than the low moods.

D007-D005_h022.question:
I’ve been living here in the nursing home since my Al dies ten years back, and things have gotten real hard since my mind started playing tricks. For over a year and a half now, I keep seeing signs—my sweetheart, Mr. Calloway from Chapel Hill—he’s not alive, but I *know* he’s been sneaking around with that nurse, the blonde one with the perfume. I used to talk quicker, but now it takes me time to answer. I sleep poor—same dream over and over: Al dragging me through the cornfield, yelling. But these low moods, the slow talk—they come and go. D007-D005_h022.options:

    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D005_h023.question:
I’ve been working at City Hall for over twenty years—records department—so I used to keep things neat, on time. But… it’s been hard. For about a year and a half now, I’ve felt like something’s off. There’s this woman—I know she’s watching me. She works in permits, doesn’t say much, but I *know* she’s in love with me. I see it in the way she leaves papers slightly shifted on my desk. She doesn’t have to speak—it’s all coded.

Talking’s harder now, I guess. My thoughts… they don’t line up right. Sometimes I say things and even *I* don’t get them afterward. My wife says I just stare or grunt when she asks me to do simple things, like turn off the light. Not because I don’t want to—just feels like my body won’t listen.

My voice is slow, I know. I can feel the words dragging. I’ve cried a few times outta nowhere, especially at night when I can’t sleep—take hours to fall into bed. But those low moods? They come and go. Not all the time. Mostly, it’s the voices—whispers when no one’s there, saying she’s in danger, that I have to protect her. That lasts almost every day. The sadness… that’s only there once in a while.
D007-D005_h023.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D005_h024.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year and a half. At first, I thought it was burnout—working long hours at the gym, pushing clients and myself. But things changed. I started smelling something… like rotting meat, but no one else notices. I know it sounds crazy, but it's real to me. I also became convinced the world is ending—like, actually collapsing soon. Not climate change or war, but just… vanishing. Everything. Me, the city, all of it—gone.  

People say I don’t finish thoughts. I *try*, but my mind drifts. Sometimes I catch myself copying guys at the gym—like mirroring their stretches without meaning to. I used to love training, but now just getting dressed feels like climbing a mountain. I stay in bed. Moving is slow. I barely text friends.  

The sadness came later, I think—maybe a year ago. Nightmares too—drowning in black sludge, waking up gasping. But it’s not like I’m sad *all* the time. It comes in waves. The voices, the smells, the belief the world is dissolving—that’s been constant. The heaviness, the tears—that’s only part of it. It’s like the dark moods dip in and out, but the breaking-apart feeling? That never leaves.
D007-D005_h024.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D005_h025.question:
I’ve been a high school teacher for over ten years, and honestly, I can’t remember the last time I felt like myself. Lately, everything feels… off. For the past year and a half, I’ve been convinced the world is ending—like, literally crumbling. Not in a metaphorical way. I taste metal all the time, even when I’m not eating anything. It’s like someone poisoned the air. I’ve tried explaining this to my principal, but I went off on some tangent about government signals in the water, and he just stared at me. I didn’t even answer his question about grading.

There are days I just sit in my classroom after school, frozen. No energy to move. My students say hi, and I don’t respond. Not because I don’t care—because it all feels pointless. Nothing matters. I used to love coaching debate, but now even that feels empty. I haven’t gone out with friends in forever. Honestly, nothing brings joy anymore.

I’ve been having nightmares too—vivid ones—about floods swallowing the school. I pace my apartment all night, rubbing my hands raw. But these low moods? They come and go. The paranoia, the voices, the taste of rust—that’s what’s constant. The sadness is just… there sometimes.
D007-D005_h025.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
